text: fikih fiqih Ba ‘Alawi Lineage: The Prophet’s Descendants and Da‘wah in the Nusantara The Prophet’s ﷺ lineage through Sayyidah Fatimah and Sayyidina Husain, Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir’s migration to Hadramaut, the emergence of Habaib family names, and their role in the Nusantara. The Prophet’s ﷺ continuing lineage is through his daughter Sayyidah Fatimah al-Zahra and her husband Sayyidina Ali ibn Abi Talib. Their descendants branched through Sayyidina Hasan, commonly associated with the title Sharif, and Sayyidina Husain, whose descendants are commonly known as Sayyids or Habaib. The Husaini line continued through Ali Zainal Abidin (As-Sajjad), who survived Karbala, then Muhammad al-Baqir, Ja‘far al-Sadiq, Ali al-Uraidhi, and Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir. The lesson places his migration from Basrah to Hadramaut around 317 AH amid political turmoil. The Ba ‘Alawi name is traced to Alawi ibn Ubaidillah ibn Ahmad al-Muhajir. Muhammad al-Faqih al-Muqaddam (d. 653 AH) is associated with the symbolic laying down of the sword and a path of da‘wah grounded in scholarship, spiritual discipline, and good character. Ba ‘Alawi descendants established family branches including Assegaf, Al-Attas, Al-Habsyi, Al-Haddad, Alaydrus, Shihab, Al-Jufri, Bin Yahya, and Al-Kaff, among others. Lineage records are preserved through family genealogies and, in Indonesia, recorded by Maktab Daimi of Rabithah Alawiyah. “Sayyid” refers to lineage; “Habib” is an honorific used for a Sayyid known for knowledge and piety. Love and honor the Prophet’s family with proper manners and without excess (ghuluw). Follow their examples of knowledge, character, and gentle da‘wah. Examples of Habaib in Indonesia: Figures, Family Names, and Verification A selection of Indonesian scholars and preachers publicly known by the title Habib. This is not a complete list and does not replace individual lineage verification. Historical figures: Habib Ali bin Abdurrahman Al-Habsyi (Habib Ali Kwitang) and Habib Salim bin Ahmad Jindan are known in the history of Islamic teaching in Indonesia. Contemporary scholars and preachers: Habib Muhammad Luthfi bin Ali bin Yahya, Habib Syech bin Abdul Qodir Assegaf, and Habib Jindan bin Novel bin Salim Jindan. Other public figures known by the title include Habib Munzir bin Fuad Al-Musawa (founder of Majelis Rasulullah), Habib Muhammad Rizieq Shihab, and Habib Bahar bin Ali bin Smith (also written Sumayt or Sumait). Public titles and family names do not by themselves prove an individual’s genealogy. For a family’s lineage status, consult the records and verification process of Maktab Daimi Rabithah Alawiyah. Do not assume that everyone with the Shihab or Smith surname uses the title Habib. Women from families recorded as Alawiyyin are commonly referred to as Syarifah; usage follows each family’s tradition. When referring to a figure, distinguish public titles, family names, and individually verified lineage. Use reliable sources and do not generalize about a family from its surname. Seeking Treatment and Preserving Life (Hifz al-Nafs) Protecting health and seeking care when ill can be part of worship and trust in Allah. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged seeking treatment (Sunan Abi Dawud 3855). The hadith encourages care; it does not promise that every illness has a known or guaranteed cure. Preserving life (hifz al-nafs) is one of the five higher objectives of Islamic law (maqasid al-shariah). Seeking care is compatible with tawakkul: it means taking reasonable steps and consulting qualified health professionals. The International Islamic Fiqh Academy says treatment can be obligatory when foregoing it risks death, loss of an organ or function, disability, or transmission; recommended when there is meaningful benefit without those risks; permissible in other cases; and disliked when the treatment risk is greater than the condition being treated. Assessing need and risk is a clinical matter. A health professional should explain the diagnosis, prognosis, likely benefits, side effects, and alternatives. A capable patient should be informed and give consent. Emergency care follows applicable clinical and legal rules. This summary does not diagnose or tell anyone to start, stop, or change medication. Make treatment decisions with the clinician responsible for care. If you are unwell, seek an assessment from a qualified health professional. Ask about benefits, risks, alternatives, and warning signs; do not delay emergency care or change treatment on your own. Necessity Principles for Medicines and Treatment Shariah concessions for medical ingredients are conditional and limited to the actual need. The legal maxim “necessity permits prohibited matters” is supported in a specific context by Qur’an 2:173, which also limits the concession to necessity without desire for excess or transgression. A limiting maxim says that necessity is measured according to its extent. This is not a blanket permission for every product whose ingredients or status are uncertain. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 says medicines should ordinarily use pure and halal ingredients. It describes an exception for necessity or an equivalent life-threatening need when no halal and pure ingredient is available and a competent, trusted medical professional recommends it because no halal medicine is available. A person should not declare a situation medically necessary based only on an ingredient list or social-media claim. Clinicians assess the medical need and alternatives; qualified scholars or fatwa bodies address the religious ruling. If a suitable halal and pure alternative becomes available, reassess whether the concession still applies. Discuss any change with a doctor or pharmacist; do not abruptly stop treatment without clinical advice. MUI gives separate details for external-use medicines. The ruling depends on the ingredient, route of use, medical need, and applicable fatwa. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about the medicine’s ingredients and status, suitable alternatives, and the risks of switching or delaying treatment. For a religious ruling, consult MUI guidance or a scholar familiar with medical questions. More Muslim Scholars: Medicine, Mathematics, Engineering, and Mapping Selected scholars from different periods and regions who worked in medicine, pharmacy, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy, mechanical engineering, and geography. Medicine and surgery: Al-Razi wrote clinical and medical works; Al-Zahrawi compiled al-Tasrif, a medical encyclopedia with a major section on surgery; Ibn al-Nafis described blood passing through the lungs and rejected the idea that it crossed the heart’s ventricular septum; Ibn al-Baytar compiled a major work on medicinal substances and plants. Mathematics, astronomy, and natural sciences: Al-Kindi wrote on mathematics and several sciences; Nasir al-Din al-Tusi developed astronomical and mathematical work and worked at the Maragha Observatory. Their work grew through translation, debate, and development across generations. Philosophy and music: Al-Farabi is known for works on logic, philosophy, and music; Ibn Rushd wrote philosophical commentaries and also worked in medicine, law, and religious scholarship in al-Andalus. Mechanical engineering: Al-Jazari described mechanical devices, water clocks, and automata in his Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. His work shows the combination of design, practical knowledge, and workshop skill in his era. Geography and cartography: Al-Idrisi compiled geographical works and a world map for the court of Sicily in the twelfth century, drawing on the geographical knowledge and travel accounts available in his time. This is a selection, not a ranking or complete list. Labels such as “first inventor” or “father of modern science” need care: scientific achievements often developed gradually, building on earlier work and involving networks across languages and faiths. Choose one scholar and explore an original work or reliable history-of-science study. Note the field, work, historical context, and what the sources actually support without overstating the claim. • : ↗ 1. Kondisi gawat darurat mengikuti ketentuan klinis dan hukum yang berlaku. Care-seeking and preservation of life Health concern or need Assessment by a qualified health professional Discuss diagnosis, benefits, risks, and alternatives Serious harm if untreated Treatment may be obligatory under the IIFA resolution Meaningful benefit without severe threat Treatment may be recommended or permissible, depending on the case Risks outweigh expected benefit Weigh the risks and seek another clinical opinion when appropriate Patients should receive an explanation and give consent when able. Emergencies follow applicable clinical and legal rules. Bagan menilai keringanan obat saat darurat Terapi dibutuhkan secara klinis Periksa bahan dan alternatif halal serta suci Alternatif yang sesuai tersedia Gunakan alternatif tersebut; alasan darurat perlu ditinjau kembali. Belum ada alternatif yang sesuai Tenaga medis kompeten menilai kebutuhan dan merekomendasikan terapi. Fatwa MUI No. 30/2013 menyebut kondisi darurat atau kebutuhan setara darurat yang mengancam jiwa, belum adanya bahan halal dan suci, serta rekomendasi tenaga medis kompeten dan tepercaya. Assessing a medicine exception in necessity Treatment is clinically needed Check ingredients and suitable halal, pure alternatives A suitable alternative is available Use that alternative; reassess whether necessity still applies. No suitable alternative is available A qualified health professional assesses the need and recommends treatment. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 describes necessity or equivalent life-threatening need, no halal and pure alternative, and a recommendation from a competent, trusted medical professional. Purification of the Heart Learn to purify the heart, renew your intentions, and build good habits in daily life. These exercises are for reflection, not a measure of spiritual purity or a prescription of fixed practice counts. References are paraphrased. Fiqh of Worship A basic guide to purification, prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage, and everyday worship. Practical summaries follow the Shafi‘i school where specific details are discussed. The cited evidence gives general foundations, not every legal detail. Study special cases and differences among schools with a qualified teacher. Prophetic Biography Follow the Prophet’s ﷺ life from Makkah to the end of his life and reflect on its lessons in character. Events are arranged chronologically. Common Era dates are approximate, and some dates are disputed. Quranic and hadith references support the event or its lesson, not necessarily its exact date. Arabic Rhetoric (Balaghah) Study how expression fits meaning through grammar, morphology, ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘, with examples from the Qur’an. This introduction draws on general discussions of ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘ and translations of Al-Balaghah al-Wadihah. Quranic rhetorical interpretation and its details should be taught and checked by a teacher; this summary does not replace a text or class. Islamic Marriage and Family Law A guide to engagement, marriage essentials, the mahr, spouses’ rights and duties, conflict resolution, and child custody. Based on summaries of Shafi‘i and majority-school family jurisprudence. Quranic and authentic hadith evidence is included as legal and ethical reference. Integrity and Anti-Corruption Islamic rulings on public trust, bribery, improper gifts, corruption, and protecting public wealth. Islam regards corruption as a grave sin that damages social justice. This material summarizes Quranic and authentic hadith evidence against unlawfully consuming public wealth. Islamic Transactions and Finance A guide to lawful earnings, riba, gharar, debts, Islamic business contracts, and contemporary services such as pay-later, online lending, and e-commerce. A foundational principle is that transactions are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material follows DSN-MUI guidance and contemporary Islamic commercial jurisprudence. Halal Food and Wholesome Living A guide to land and sea animals, Islamic slaughter, intoxicants and drugs, and critical points in processed foods. A foundational principle is that foods are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material refers to LPPOM MUI halal standards and Shafi‘i jurisprudence. Islamic Medical Ethics and Contemporary Medicine Islamic guidance on seeking treatment, emergencies, blood and organ donation, euthanasia, IVF, and autopsies. An introduction based on MUI and International Islamic Fiqh Academy guidance and the objective of protecting life. Educational only: it is not a diagnosis or a substitute for advice from a doctor, pharmacist, or qualified scholar about an individual case. Comparative Religion: Tawhid and the Prophethood of Jesus A study of arguments for God’s oneness, the status of Jesus, Quranic and Biblical texts, the history of the Trinity, and prophecies of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Prepared from Quranic text, authentic hadith, Biblical quotations, and academic work in Christology. It aims to strengthen Islamic belief while supporting respectful, evidence-based interfaith dialogue. The Qur’an, Modern Science, and Natural Law Explore natural laws, relativity, Big Bang cosmology, the expanding universe, embryology, the water cycle, and ecological balance through Quranic signs. Draws on Quranic signs and established findings in physics, astronomy, and biology. It aims to encourage reflection on faith and creation. Islamic Creed and the Hereafter Study the pillars of faith, divine oneness and attributes, angels and the unseen, destiny, the Last Day, the grave, judgment, the bridge, Paradise, and Hell. Based on core Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama‘ah teachings and evidence from the Qur’an and authentic hadith. The aim is to strengthen faith and spiritual readiness for the Hereafter. Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence Learn the sources of Islamic law, why the four schools differ, and the five major legal maxims. Based on classical works such as Al-Waraqat by Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni and Shafi‘i legal maxims. The aim is to explain legal reasoning and encourage fairness toward legitimate scholarly disagreement. Hadith Studies and Authentication Understand hadith criticism, the structure of chains and texts, authentic and fabricated reports, and methods for checking narrations. Hadith terminology provides a rigorous method for evaluating historical reports and preserving the Prophetic message. The Golden Age of Islamic Civilization Explore global Muslim scholarship and civilization, from Baghdad’s House of Wisdom and al-Andalus to scholars who helped shape modern science. The centuries from the eighth to fourteenth CE show how Quranic learning and scientific and technological work flourished alongside one another. Islamic Parenting and Family Psychology Practical parenting guidance from the Qur’an and Sunnah: Luqman’s advice, child development, empathetic communication, digital safety, and family wellbeing. Children are a trust and are born upon a pure disposition. Islamic parenting nurtures them through loving example, prayer, and gentleness, not demands for obedience alone. Quranic Studies and Tafsir Methodology Study the compilation of the Qur’an, Makkan and Madinan passages, occasions of revelation, abrogation, and sound methods of interpretation. Quranic studies help readers understand revelation responsibly and guard against subjective readings or forcing a text into a context. Islamic Inheritance Law A guide to inheritance essentials, conditions and impediments, fixed-share heirs and residuaries, the 2:1 ratio, bequests, gifts, and dispute resolution. Inheritance law provides a framework for fair distribution of family wealth and helps prevent conflict. Digital Etiquette and Online Conduct Learn the manners of seeking knowledge online, responsible social media use, guarding speech, privacy, online backbiting, showing off, and digital copyright. In a fast-moving digital world, good manners and integrity distinguish mindful conduct from behavior driven by algorithms. Muslim Women: Exemplars and Fiqh Learn from the leadership, scholarship, and service of notable early Muslim women, alongside guidance on worship, menstruation, and women’s rights. Islam recognizes women’s independent property rights, access to knowledge, and meaningful contributions to society. Higher Objectives of Sharia and Governance Study the five higher objectives of Islamic law, the Constitution of Madinah, criminal law principles, consultation, and public leadership. Islamic law seeks genuine public benefit and aims to prevent oppression and harm for all people. End-Times Trials: The Dajjal and the Return of Jesus Study authentic reports about end-times trials, the Dajjal’s traits and deception, the Mahdi, the Dajjal’s defeat, and protections for believers. Studying end-times trials is not for panic or speculative predictions. It should strengthen tawhid, guard against confusion, and encourage good deeds. Stories of the Prophets and Messengers Follow the stories of the 25 prophets and messengers and the account of Khidr, exploring prophetic lineage, miracles, the five Messengers of steadfast resolve, and lessons in da‘wah. The prophetic stories are more than accounts of the past: they offer examples of character, steadfast faith, and the preservation of revelation. Islam in the Indonesian Archipelago, Walisongo, and Habaib Lineages Explore Islam’s peaceful spread through the spice routes and Samudera Pasai, Walisongo’s approach to local culture, Ba ‘Alawi lineage, maritime kingdoms, and pesantren traditions. Islam in the Nusantara spread through trade, diplomacy, good character, and culturally aware teaching. The Ten Companions Promised Paradise Learn from the character, sacrifice, and leadership of ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise by the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions were the finest generation of this community. Their integrity and sincerity offer guidance for preserving faith amid later trials. Islamic Environmental Ethics Care for the Earth as a trust: water conservation, animal welfare, tree planting, preventing environmental harm, and sustainable stewardship. Today’s ecological crisis is not only scientific and technological; it is also a moral and spiritual challenge. Islam makes care for creation part of faithful stewardship. Islamic Da‘wah and Interfaith Communication Study Quranic persuasive communication, audience awareness, respectful interfaith dialogue, and service through action. Da‘wah is not coercion or condemnation. It conveys truth with wisdom, sound reasoning, gentle character, and respectful argument. Angels, Jinn, and the Unseen Learn about angels, jinn, satanic deception, the intermediate realm, and authentic Islamic spiritual protection. This material supports sound belief and guards against shirk, superstition, fortune-telling, and occult claims through the Qur’an and Sunnah. Scholarly Disagreement and Religious Moderation Understand why legal schools differ, the etiquette of disagreement, wasatiyyah, and ways to preserve Muslim unity. This course encourages broad understanding and patience in subsidiary matters, while avoiding blind partisanship and reckless accusations of disbelief. thaharah Thaharah: hadas dan najis Bersuci Bedakan keadaan hadas dengan najis pada badan, pakaian, atau tempat. Hadas kecil diangkat dengan wudhu; hadas besar dengan mandi wajib. Najis dibersihkan sesuai jenisnya hingga hilang sifat najis yang dapat dihilangkan. Gunakan air suci yang menyucikan dan pastikan tidak ada penghalang air pada anggota bersuci. Periksa kebersihan pakaian dan tempat sebelum shalat. 5/6 wudhu Enam rukun wudhu Bersuci Pelajari bagian wajib wudhu menurut mazhab Syafi’i. Niat ketika mulai membasuh wajah; basuh seluruh batas wajah. Basuh kedua tangan termasuk siku, lalu usap sebagian kepala. Basuh kedua kaki termasuk mata kaki, dan lakukan berurutan (tertib). Basmalah, berkumur, dan mengulang basuhan tiga kali termasuk sunnah, bukan pengganti rukun. Praktikkan berurutan dan periksa siku, tumit, serta sela jari. NU Online — Mengenal Rukun Wudhu (Syafi’i) batal-wudhu Pembatal wudhu Bersuci Kenali keadaan yang mengharuskan berwudhu kembali. Keluar sesuatu dari qubul atau dubur dan hilang kesadaran termasuk pembatal. Dalam Syafi’i, tidur dengan pantat tidak tetap pada tempat duduk membatalkan wudhu. Sentuhan kulit lawan jenis bukan mahram tanpa penghalang pada usia yang memenuhi ketentuan, serta menyentuh kemaluan manusia dengan bagian dalam telapak/jari, memiliki rincian pembatal dalam Syafi’i. Ragu semata tidak membatalkan keyakinan sudah suci. Bedakan kejadian pasti yang membatalkan dengan keraguan. mandi Mandi wajib Bersuci Mandi wajib mengangkat hadas besar. Janabah serta berakhirnya haid atau nifas merupakan sebab mandi wajib. Niat saat mulai membasuh tubuh dan ratakan air ke seluruh kulit serta rambut. Bersihkan najis dan penghalang air; perhatikan lipatan tubuh serta pangkal rambut. Susun urutan mandi yang memastikan seluruh tubuh terkena air. 5/6 tayamum Tayamum dan keringanan bersuci Bersuci Tayamum disyariatkan ketika air tidak tersedia atau tidak dapat digunakan dengan alasan yang sah. Dalam Syafi’i, gunakan debu suci, berniat, usap wajah dan kedua tangan sampai siku secara tertib. Tayamum untuk shalat fardhu dilakukan setelah masuk waktunya dan memenuhi ketentuan pencarian air. Satu tayamum digunakan untuk satu shalat fardhu; rincian sakit dan perban perlu bimbingan. text: akhlak penyucian jiwa Ba ‘Alawi Lineage: The Prophet’s Descendants and Da‘wah in the Nusantara The Prophet’s ﷺ lineage through Sayyidah Fatimah and Sayyidina Husain, Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir’s migration to Hadramaut, the emergence of Habaib family names, and their role in the Nusantara. The Prophet’s ﷺ continuing lineage is through his daughter Sayyidah Fatimah al-Zahra and her husband Sayyidina Ali ibn Abi Talib. Their descendants branched through Sayyidina Hasan, commonly associated with the title Sharif, and Sayyidina Husain, whose descendants are commonly known as Sayyids or Habaib. The Husaini line continued through Ali Zainal Abidin (As-Sajjad), who survived Karbala, then Muhammad al-Baqir, Ja‘far al-Sadiq, Ali al-Uraidhi, and Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir. The lesson places his migration from Basrah to Hadramaut around 317 AH amid political turmoil. The Ba ‘Alawi name is traced to Alawi ibn Ubaidillah ibn Ahmad al-Muhajir. Muhammad al-Faqih al-Muqaddam (d. 653 AH) is associated with the symbolic laying down of the sword and a path of da‘wah grounded in scholarship, spiritual discipline, and good character. Ba ‘Alawi descendants established family branches including Assegaf, Al-Attas, Al-Habsyi, Al-Haddad, Alaydrus, Shihab, Al-Jufri, Bin Yahya, and Al-Kaff, among others. Lineage records are preserved through family genealogies and, in Indonesia, recorded by Maktab Daimi of Rabithah Alawiyah. “Sayyid” refers to lineage; “Habib” is an honorific used for a Sayyid known for knowledge and piety. Love and honor the Prophet’s family with proper manners and without excess (ghuluw). Follow their examples of knowledge, character, and gentle da‘wah. Examples of Habaib in Indonesia: Figures, Family Names, and Verification A selection of Indonesian scholars and preachers publicly known by the title Habib. This is not a complete list and does not replace individual lineage verification. Historical figures: Habib Ali bin Abdurrahman Al-Habsyi (Habib Ali Kwitang) and Habib Salim bin Ahmad Jindan are known in the history of Islamic teaching in Indonesia. Contemporary scholars and preachers: Habib Muhammad Luthfi bin Ali bin Yahya, Habib Syech bin Abdul Qodir Assegaf, and Habib Jindan bin Novel bin Salim Jindan. Other public figures known by the title include Habib Munzir bin Fuad Al-Musawa (founder of Majelis Rasulullah), Habib Muhammad Rizieq Shihab, and Habib Bahar bin Ali bin Smith (also written Sumayt or Sumait). Public titles and family names do not by themselves prove an individual’s genealogy. For a family’s lineage status, consult the records and verification process of Maktab Daimi Rabithah Alawiyah. Do not assume that everyone with the Shihab or Smith surname uses the title Habib. Women from families recorded as Alawiyyin are commonly referred to as Syarifah; usage follows each family’s tradition. When referring to a figure, distinguish public titles, family names, and individually verified lineage. Use reliable sources and do not generalize about a family from its surname. Seeking Treatment and Preserving Life (Hifz al-Nafs) Protecting health and seeking care when ill can be part of worship and trust in Allah. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged seeking treatment (Sunan Abi Dawud 3855). The hadith encourages care; it does not promise that every illness has a known or guaranteed cure. Preserving life (hifz al-nafs) is one of the five higher objectives of Islamic law (maqasid al-shariah). Seeking care is compatible with tawakkul: it means taking reasonable steps and consulting qualified health professionals. The International Islamic Fiqh Academy says treatment can be obligatory when foregoing it risks death, loss of an organ or function, disability, or transmission; recommended when there is meaningful benefit without those risks; permissible in other cases; and disliked when the treatment risk is greater than the condition being treated. Assessing need and risk is a clinical matter. A health professional should explain the diagnosis, prognosis, likely benefits, side effects, and alternatives. A capable patient should be informed and give consent. Emergency care follows applicable clinical and legal rules. This summary does not diagnose or tell anyone to start, stop, or change medication. Make treatment decisions with the clinician responsible for care. If you are unwell, seek an assessment from a qualified health professional. Ask about benefits, risks, alternatives, and warning signs; do not delay emergency care or change treatment on your own. Necessity Principles for Medicines and Treatment Shariah concessions for medical ingredients are conditional and limited to the actual need. The legal maxim “necessity permits prohibited matters” is supported in a specific context by Qur’an 2:173, which also limits the concession to necessity without desire for excess or transgression. A limiting maxim says that necessity is measured according to its extent. This is not a blanket permission for every product whose ingredients or status are uncertain. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 says medicines should ordinarily use pure and halal ingredients. It describes an exception for necessity or an equivalent life-threatening need when no halal and pure ingredient is available and a competent, trusted medical professional recommends it because no halal medicine is available. A person should not declare a situation medically necessary based only on an ingredient list or social-media claim. Clinicians assess the medical need and alternatives; qualified scholars or fatwa bodies address the religious ruling. If a suitable halal and pure alternative becomes available, reassess whether the concession still applies. Discuss any change with a doctor or pharmacist; do not abruptly stop treatment without clinical advice. MUI gives separate details for external-use medicines. The ruling depends on the ingredient, route of use, medical need, and applicable fatwa. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about the medicine’s ingredients and status, suitable alternatives, and the risks of switching or delaying treatment. For a religious ruling, consult MUI guidance or a scholar familiar with medical questions. More Muslim Scholars: Medicine, Mathematics, Engineering, and Mapping Selected scholars from different periods and regions who worked in medicine, pharmacy, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy, mechanical engineering, and geography. Medicine and surgery: Al-Razi wrote clinical and medical works; Al-Zahrawi compiled al-Tasrif, a medical encyclopedia with a major section on surgery; Ibn al-Nafis described blood passing through the lungs and rejected the idea that it crossed the heart’s ventricular septum; Ibn al-Baytar compiled a major work on medicinal substances and plants. Mathematics, astronomy, and natural sciences: Al-Kindi wrote on mathematics and several sciences; Nasir al-Din al-Tusi developed astronomical and mathematical work and worked at the Maragha Observatory. Their work grew through translation, debate, and development across generations. Philosophy and music: Al-Farabi is known for works on logic, philosophy, and music; Ibn Rushd wrote philosophical commentaries and also worked in medicine, law, and religious scholarship in al-Andalus. Mechanical engineering: Al-Jazari described mechanical devices, water clocks, and automata in his Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. His work shows the combination of design, practical knowledge, and workshop skill in his era. Geography and cartography: Al-Idrisi compiled geographical works and a world map for the court of Sicily in the twelfth century, drawing on the geographical knowledge and travel accounts available in his time. This is a selection, not a ranking or complete list. Labels such as “first inventor” or “father of modern science” need care: scientific achievements often developed gradually, building on earlier work and involving networks across languages and faiths. Choose one scholar and explore an original work or reliable history-of-science study. Note the field, work, historical context, and what the sources actually support without overstating the claim. • : ↗ 1. Kondisi gawat darurat mengikuti ketentuan klinis dan hukum yang berlaku. Care-seeking and preservation of life Health concern or need Assessment by a qualified health professional Discuss diagnosis, benefits, risks, and alternatives Serious harm if untreated Treatment may be obligatory under the IIFA resolution Meaningful benefit without severe threat Treatment may be recommended or permissible, depending on the case Risks outweigh expected benefit Weigh the risks and seek another clinical opinion when appropriate Patients should receive an explanation and give consent when able. Emergencies follow applicable clinical and legal rules. Bagan menilai keringanan obat saat darurat Terapi dibutuhkan secara klinis Periksa bahan dan alternatif halal serta suci Alternatif yang sesuai tersedia Gunakan alternatif tersebut; alasan darurat perlu ditinjau kembali. Belum ada alternatif yang sesuai Tenaga medis kompeten menilai kebutuhan dan merekomendasikan terapi. Fatwa MUI No. 30/2013 menyebut kondisi darurat atau kebutuhan setara darurat yang mengancam jiwa, belum adanya bahan halal dan suci, serta rekomendasi tenaga medis kompeten dan tepercaya. Assessing a medicine exception in necessity Treatment is clinically needed Check ingredients and suitable halal, pure alternatives A suitable alternative is available Use that alternative; reassess whether necessity still applies. No suitable alternative is available A qualified health professional assesses the need and recommends treatment. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 describes necessity or equivalent life-threatening need, no halal and pure alternative, and a recommendation from a competent, trusted medical professional. Al-Razi Al-Zahrawi Ibn al-Nafis Ibn al-Baytar Al-Kindi Nasir al-Din al-Tusi Al-Farabi Ibn Rushd (Averroes) Al-Jazari Al-Idrisi Bersuci dan kebersihan Wudhu Menjaga wudhu Mandi wajib Tayamum Shalat Shalat berjamaah Keringanan shalat Puasa Ramadan Zakat Haji dan umrah Pengurusan jenazah Purification and cleanliness Wudu Maintaining wudu Ghusl Tayammum Prayer Congregational prayer Prayer concessions Ramadan fasting Hajj and Umrah Funeral care . Purification of the Heart Learn to purify the heart, renew your intentions, and build good habits in daily life. These exercises are for reflection, not a measure of spiritual purity or a prescription of fixed practice counts. References are paraphrased. Fiqh of Worship A basic guide to purification, prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage, and everyday worship. Practical summaries follow the Shafi‘i school where specific details are discussed. The cited evidence gives general foundations, not every legal detail. Study special cases and differences among schools with a qualified teacher. Prophetic Biography Follow the Prophet’s ﷺ life from Makkah to the end of his life and reflect on its lessons in character. Events are arranged chronologically. Common Era dates are approximate, and some dates are disputed. Quranic and hadith references support the event or its lesson, not necessarily its exact date. Arabic Rhetoric (Balaghah) Study how expression fits meaning through grammar, morphology, ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘, with examples from the Qur’an. This introduction draws on general discussions of ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘ and translations of Al-Balaghah al-Wadihah. Quranic rhetorical interpretation and its details should be taught and checked by a teacher; this summary does not replace a text or class. Islamic Marriage and Family Law A guide to engagement, marriage essentials, the mahr, spouses’ rights and duties, conflict resolution, and child custody. Based on summaries of Shafi‘i and majority-school family jurisprudence. Quranic and authentic hadith evidence is included as legal and ethical reference. Integrity and Anti-Corruption Islamic rulings on public trust, bribery, improper gifts, corruption, and protecting public wealth. Islam regards corruption as a grave sin that damages social justice. This material summarizes Quranic and authentic hadith evidence against unlawfully consuming public wealth. Islamic Transactions and Finance A guide to lawful earnings, riba, gharar, debts, Islamic business contracts, and contemporary services such as pay-later, online lending, and e-commerce. A foundational principle is that transactions are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material follows DSN-MUI guidance and contemporary Islamic commercial jurisprudence. Halal Food and Wholesome Living A guide to land and sea animals, Islamic slaughter, intoxicants and drugs, and critical points in processed foods. A foundational principle is that foods are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material refers to LPPOM MUI halal standards and Shafi‘i jurisprudence. Islamic Medical Ethics and Contemporary Medicine Islamic guidance on seeking treatment, emergencies, blood and organ donation, euthanasia, IVF, and autopsies. An introduction based on MUI and International Islamic Fiqh Academy guidance and the objective of protecting life. Educational only: it is not a diagnosis or a substitute for advice from a doctor, pharmacist, or qualified scholar about an individual case. Comparative Religion: Tawhid and the Prophethood of Jesus A study of arguments for God’s oneness, the status of Jesus, Quranic and Biblical texts, the history of the Trinity, and prophecies of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Prepared from Quranic text, authentic hadith, Biblical quotations, and academic work in Christology. It aims to strengthen Islamic belief while supporting respectful, evidence-based interfaith dialogue. The Qur’an, Modern Science, and Natural Law Explore natural laws, relativity, Big Bang cosmology, the expanding universe, embryology, the water cycle, and ecological balance through Quranic signs. Draws on Quranic signs and established findings in physics, astronomy, and biology. It aims to encourage reflection on faith and creation. Islamic Creed and the Hereafter Study the pillars of faith, divine oneness and attributes, angels and the unseen, destiny, the Last Day, the grave, judgment, the bridge, Paradise, and Hell. Based on core Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama‘ah teachings and evidence from the Qur’an and authentic hadith. The aim is to strengthen faith and spiritual readiness for the Hereafter. Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence Learn the sources of Islamic law, why the four schools differ, and the five major legal maxims. Based on classical works such as Al-Waraqat by Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni and Shafi‘i legal maxims. The aim is to explain legal reasoning and encourage fairness toward legitimate scholarly disagreement. Hadith Studies and Authentication Understand hadith criticism, the structure of chains and texts, authentic and fabricated reports, and methods for checking narrations. Hadith terminology provides a rigorous method for evaluating historical reports and preserving the Prophetic message. The Golden Age of Islamic Civilization Explore global Muslim scholarship and civilization, from Baghdad’s House of Wisdom and al-Andalus to scholars who helped shape modern science. The centuries from the eighth to fourteenth CE show how Quranic learning and scientific and technological work flourished alongside one another. Islamic Parenting and Family Psychology Practical parenting guidance from the Qur’an and Sunnah: Luqman’s advice, child development, empathetic communication, digital safety, and family wellbeing. Children are a trust and are born upon a pure disposition. Islamic parenting nurtures them through loving example, prayer, and gentleness, not demands for obedience alone. Quranic Studies and Tafsir Methodology Study the compilation of the Qur’an, Makkan and Madinan passages, occasions of revelation, abrogation, and sound methods of interpretation. Quranic studies help readers understand revelation responsibly and guard against subjective readings or forcing a text into a context. Islamic Inheritance Law A guide to inheritance essentials, conditions and impediments, fixed-share heirs and residuaries, the 2:1 ratio, bequests, gifts, and dispute resolution. Inheritance law provides a framework for fair distribution of family wealth and helps prevent conflict. Digital Etiquette and Online Conduct Learn the manners of seeking knowledge online, responsible social media use, guarding speech, privacy, online backbiting, showing off, and digital copyright. In a fast-moving digital world, good manners and integrity distinguish mindful conduct from behavior driven by algorithms. Muslim Women: Exemplars and Fiqh Learn from the leadership, scholarship, and service of notable early Muslim women, alongside guidance on worship, menstruation, and women’s rights. Islam recognizes women’s independent property rights, access to knowledge, and meaningful contributions to society. Higher Objectives of Sharia and Governance Study the five higher objectives of Islamic law, the Constitution of Madinah, criminal law principles, consultation, and public leadership. Islamic law seeks genuine public benefit and aims to prevent oppression and harm for all people. End-Times Trials: The Dajjal and the Return of Jesus Study authentic reports about end-times trials, the Dajjal’s traits and deception, the Mahdi, the Dajjal’s defeat, and protections for believers. Studying end-times trials is not for panic or speculative predictions. It should strengthen tawhid, guard against confusion, and encourage good deeds. Stories of the Prophets and Messengers Follow the stories of the 25 prophets and messengers and the account of Khidr, exploring prophetic lineage, miracles, the five Messengers of steadfast resolve, and lessons in da‘wah. The prophetic stories are more than accounts of the past: they offer examples of character, steadfast faith, and the preservation of revelation. Islam in the Indonesian Archipelago, Walisongo, and Habaib Lineages Explore Islam’s peaceful spread through the spice routes and Samudera Pasai, Walisongo’s approach to local culture, Ba ‘Alawi lineage, maritime kingdoms, and pesantren traditions. Islam in the Nusantara spread through trade, diplomacy, good character, and culturally aware teaching. The Ten Companions Promised Paradise Learn from the character, sacrifice, and leadership of ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise by the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions were the finest generation of this community. Their integrity and sincerity offer guidance for preserving faith amid later trials. Islamic Environmental Ethics Care for the Earth as a trust: water conservation, animal welfare, tree planting, preventing environmental harm, and sustainable stewardship. Today’s ecological crisis is not only scientific and technological; it is also a moral and spiritual challenge. Islam makes care for creation part of faithful stewardship. Islamic Da‘wah and Interfaith Communication Study Quranic persuasive communication, audience awareness, respectful interfaith dialogue, and service through action. Da‘wah is not coercion or condemnation. It conveys truth with wisdom, sound reasoning, gentle character, and respectful argument. Angels, Jinn, and the Unseen Learn about angels, jinn, satanic deception, the intermediate realm, and authentic Islamic spiritual protection. This material supports sound belief and guards against shirk, superstition, fortune-telling, and occult claims through the Qur’an and Sunnah. Scholarly Disagreement and Religious Moderation Understand why legal schools differ, the etiquette of disagreement, wasatiyyah, and ways to preserve Muslim unity. This course encourages broad understanding and patience in subsidiary matters, while avoiding blind partisanship and reckless accusations of disbelief. dasar Mengenal penyucian jiwa Landasan Tazkiyah mencakup meninggalkan keburukan dan menumbuhkan ketaatan. Kenali kebiasaan yang menjauhkan diri dari Allah dan merugikan orang lain. Perbaikan hati berjalan bersama ibadah wajib dan akhlak, bukan hanya pengalaman batin. Pilih satu kebiasaan yang ingin diperbaiki dan satu tindakan kecil penggantinya. 91/9 ikhlas Ikhlas dan menjaga niat Landasan Amal dinilai sesuai niatnya; arahkan ibadah kepada Allah. Tinggalkan dosa, sesali perbuatan, dan bertekad tidak mengulanginya. Jika menyangkut hak manusia, kembalikan hak atau selesaikan tanggung jawab dengan cara yang benar. Jangan berputus asa dari rahmat Allah. Tentukan satu tanggung jawab yang bisa mulai dibereskan hari ini. 39/53 muhasabah Muhasabah dan muraqabah Perbaikan diri Evaluasi diri dan sadari bahwa Allah mengetahui perbuatan kita. Tinjau ibadah, ucapan, dan hubungan dengan sesama secara jujur. Akhiri evaluasi dengan langkah perbaikan, bukan menyalahkan diri tanpa arah. Renungkan satu nikmat, satu kekeliruan, dan satu rencana perbaikan sebelum tidur. 59/18 sabar Sabar dan shalat Akhlak hati Kesabaran membantu bertahan dalam ketaatan dan menghadapi ujian. Sabar meliputi keteguhan berbuat baik, menahan diri dari dosa, dan menghadapi musibah. Mencari pertolongan dan menyelesaikan masalah tetap merupakan bentuk ikhtiar. Saat emosi muncul, beri jeda sebelum menjawab dan pilih ucapan yang baik. 2/153 syukur Syukur dan qanaah Akhlak hati Kenali nikmat dan gunakan untuk kebaikan. Syukur tampak dalam pengakuan hati, ucapan, dan penggunaan nikmat. Qanaah membantu merasa cukup tanpa menghentikan usaha yang halal. Sebutkan nikmat yang sering terlupakan lalu gunakan untuk membantu seseorang. 14/7 tawakal Ikhtiar dan tawakal Akhlak hati Berusaha dengan sungguh-sungguh lalu menyerahkan hasil kepada Allah. Musyawarah dan keputusan yang matang berjalan bersama tawakal. Hasil di luar kendali tidak menghapus nilai usaha yang benar. Pisahkan hal yang dapat diusahakan hari ini dari hasil yang tidak dapat dikendalikan. 3/159 penyakit-hati Riya, ujub, hasad, dan sombong Perbaikan diri Kenali dorongan mencari pujian, membanggakan diri, dan merendahkan orang. Jangan menjadikan penampilan ibadah sebagai sarana merendahkan sesama. Saat iri muncul, doakan kebaikan dan fokus memperbaiki usaha sendiri. Terima nasihat dan akui jasa orang lain. title: Sirah Nabawiyah
description: Pelajari perjalanan hidup dan keteladanan Nabi Muhammad.
text: sejarah rasul nabi Ba ‘Alawi Lineage: The Prophet’s Descendants and Da‘wah in the Nusantara The Prophet’s ﷺ lineage through Sayyidah Fatimah and Sayyidina Husain, Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir’s migration to Hadramaut, the emergence of Habaib family names, and their role in the Nusantara. The Prophet’s ﷺ continuing lineage is through his daughter Sayyidah Fatimah al-Zahra and her husband Sayyidina Ali ibn Abi Talib. Their descendants branched through Sayyidina Hasan, commonly associated with the title Sharif, and Sayyidina Husain, whose descendants are commonly known as Sayyids or Habaib. The Husaini line continued through Ali Zainal Abidin (As-Sajjad), who survived Karbala, then Muhammad al-Baqir, Ja‘far al-Sadiq, Ali al-Uraidhi, and Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir. The lesson places his migration from Basrah to Hadramaut around 317 AH amid political turmoil. The Ba ‘Alawi name is traced to Alawi ibn Ubaidillah ibn Ahmad al-Muhajir. Muhammad al-Faqih al-Muqaddam (d. 653 AH) is associated with the symbolic laying down of the sword and a path of da‘wah grounded in scholarship, spiritual discipline, and good character. Ba ‘Alawi descendants established family branches including Assegaf, Al-Attas, Al-Habsyi, Al-Haddad, Alaydrus, Shihab, Al-Jufri, Bin Yahya, and Al-Kaff, among others. Lineage records are preserved through family genealogies and, in Indonesia, recorded by Maktab Daimi of Rabithah Alawiyah. “Sayyid” refers to lineage; “Habib” is an honorific used for a Sayyid known for knowledge and piety. Love and honor the Prophet’s family with proper manners and without excess (ghuluw). Follow their examples of knowledge, character, and gentle da‘wah. Examples of Habaib in Indonesia: Figures, Family Names, and Verification A selection of Indonesian scholars and preachers publicly known by the title Habib. This is not a complete list and does not replace individual lineage verification. Historical figures: Habib Ali bin Abdurrahman Al-Habsyi (Habib Ali Kwitang) and Habib Salim bin Ahmad Jindan are known in the history of Islamic teaching in Indonesia. Contemporary scholars and preachers: Habib Muhammad Luthfi bin Ali bin Yahya, Habib Syech bin Abdul Qodir Assegaf, and Habib Jindan bin Novel bin Salim Jindan. Other public figures known by the title include Habib Munzir bin Fuad Al-Musawa (founder of Majelis Rasulullah), Habib Muhammad Rizieq Shihab, and Habib Bahar bin Ali bin Smith (also written Sumayt or Sumait). Public titles and family names do not by themselves prove an individual’s genealogy. For a family’s lineage status, consult the records and verification process of Maktab Daimi Rabithah Alawiyah. Do not assume that everyone with the Shihab or Smith surname uses the title Habib. Women from families recorded as Alawiyyin are commonly referred to as Syarifah; usage follows each family’s tradition. When referring to a figure, distinguish public titles, family names, and individually verified lineage. Use reliable sources and do not generalize about a family from its surname. Seeking Treatment and Preserving Life (Hifz al-Nafs) Protecting health and seeking care when ill can be part of worship and trust in Allah. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged seeking treatment (Sunan Abi Dawud 3855). The hadith encourages care; it does not promise that every illness has a known or guaranteed cure. Preserving life (hifz al-nafs) is one of the five higher objectives of Islamic law (maqasid al-shariah). Seeking care is compatible with tawakkul: it means taking reasonable steps and consulting qualified health professionals. The International Islamic Fiqh Academy says treatment can be obligatory when foregoing it risks death, loss of an organ or function, disability, or transmission; recommended when there is meaningful benefit without those risks; permissible in other cases; and disliked when the treatment risk is greater than the condition being treated. Assessing need and risk is a clinical matter. A health professional should explain the diagnosis, prognosis, likely benefits, side effects, and alternatives. A capable patient should be informed and give consent. Emergency care follows applicable clinical and legal rules. This summary does not diagnose or tell anyone to start, stop, or change medication. Make treatment decisions with the clinician responsible for care. If you are unwell, seek an assessment from a qualified health professional. Ask about benefits, risks, alternatives, and warning signs; do not delay emergency care or change treatment on your own. Necessity Principles for Medicines and Treatment Shariah concessions for medical ingredients are conditional and limited to the actual need. The legal maxim “necessity permits prohibited matters” is supported in a specific context by Qur’an 2:173, which also limits the concession to necessity without desire for excess or transgression. A limiting maxim says that necessity is measured according to its extent. This is not a blanket permission for every product whose ingredients or status are uncertain. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 says medicines should ordinarily use pure and halal ingredients. It describes an exception for necessity or an equivalent life-threatening need when no halal and pure ingredient is available and a competent, trusted medical professional recommends it because no halal medicine is available. A person should not declare a situation medically necessary based only on an ingredient list or social-media claim. Clinicians assess the medical need and alternatives; qualified scholars or fatwa bodies address the religious ruling. If a suitable halal and pure alternative becomes available, reassess whether the concession still applies. Discuss any change with a doctor or pharmacist; do not abruptly stop treatment without clinical advice. MUI gives separate details for external-use medicines. The ruling depends on the ingredient, route of use, medical need, and applicable fatwa. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about the medicine’s ingredients and status, suitable alternatives, and the risks of switching or delaying treatment. For a religious ruling, consult MUI guidance or a scholar familiar with medical questions. More Muslim Scholars: Medicine, Mathematics, Engineering, and Mapping Selected scholars from different periods and regions who worked in medicine, pharmacy, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy, mechanical engineering, and geography. Medicine and surgery: Al-Razi wrote clinical and medical works; Al-Zahrawi compiled al-Tasrif, a medical encyclopedia with a major section on surgery; Ibn al-Nafis described blood passing through the lungs and rejected the idea that it crossed the heart’s ventricular septum; Ibn al-Baytar compiled a major work on medicinal substances and plants. Mathematics, astronomy, and natural sciences: Al-Kindi wrote on mathematics and several sciences; Nasir al-Din al-Tusi developed astronomical and mathematical work and worked at the Maragha Observatory. Their work grew through translation, debate, and development across generations. Philosophy and music: Al-Farabi is known for works on logic, philosophy, and music; Ibn Rushd wrote philosophical commentaries and also worked in medicine, law, and religious scholarship in al-Andalus. Mechanical engineering: Al-Jazari described mechanical devices, water clocks, and automata in his Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. His work shows the combination of design, practical knowledge, and workshop skill in his era. Geography and cartography: Al-Idrisi compiled geographical works and a world map for the court of Sicily in the twelfth century, drawing on the geographical knowledge and travel accounts available in his time. This is a selection, not a ranking or complete list. Labels such as “first inventor” or “father of modern science” need care: scientific achievements often developed gradually, building on earlier work and involving networks across languages and faiths. Choose one scholar and explore an original work or reliable history-of-science study. Note the field, work, historical context, and what the sources actually support without overstating the claim. • : ↗ 1. Ba ‘Alawi and peaceful da‘wah 4. Family branches and the Nusantara network 5. Preserving lineage and titles 6. Evidence, manners, and practice Prophet Muhammad ﷺ Sharif / Ashraf Karbala · 61 AH Ja‘far al-Sadiq Ali al-Uraidhi Imam Ahmad al-Muhajir Basrah → Hadramaut · c. 317 AH Ahmad al-Muhajir Al-Faqih al-Muqaddam Sharia · tasawwuf · good character Ba ‘Alawi in Hadramaut Bin Yahya · Al-Kaff · others Scholarly and da‘wah networks in the Nusantara Syajarah ansab / family records Cross-checking and registration Qur’an 42:23 Love and honor Ahlul Bayt Without excess (ghuluw) Emulate knowledge, character, and gentle da‘wah ↓ Habib Ali bin Abdurrahman Al-Habsyi (Habib Ali Kwitang) Habib Salim bin Ahmad Jindan Habib Munzir bin Fuad Al-Musawa Habib Muhammad Luthfi bin Ali bin Yahya Habib Syech bin Abdul Qodir Assegaf Habib Jindan bin Novel bin Salim Jindan Habib Muhammad Rizieq Shihab Habib Bahar bin Ali bin Smith (Sumayt/Sumait) Bagan ikhtiar berobat dan menjaga jiwa Keluhan atau kebutuhan kesehatan Evaluasi oleh tenaga kesehatan kompeten Bahas diagnosis, manfaat, risiko, dan alternatif Risiko serius bila tidak ditangani Berobat dapat menjadi wajib menurut resolusi IIFA Manfaat nyata, tanpa ancaman berat Berobat dianjurkan atau dibolehkan sesuai keadaan Tindakan berisiko lebih besar dari manfaat Risiko perlu ditimbang; cari pendapat klinis lain bila perlu Pasien mendapat penjelasan dan memberi persetujuan bila mampu. Kondisi gawat darurat mengikuti ketentuan klinis dan hukum yang berlaku. Care-seeking and preservation of life Health concern or need Assessment by a qualified health professional Discuss diagnosis, benefits, risks, and alternatives Serious harm if untreated Treatment may be obligatory under the IIFA resolution Meaningful benefit without severe threat Treatment may be recommended or permissible, depending on the case Risks outweigh expected benefit Weigh the risks and seek another clinical opinion when appropriate Patients should receive an explanation and give consent when able. Emergencies follow applicable clinical and legal rules. Bagan menilai keringanan obat saat darurat Terapi dibutuhkan secara klinis Periksa bahan dan alternatif halal serta suci Alternatif yang sesuai tersedia Gunakan alternatif tersebut; alasan darurat perlu ditinjau kembali. Belum ada alternatif yang sesuai Tenaga medis kompeten menilai kebutuhan dan merekomendasikan terapi. Fatwa MUI No. 30/2013 menyebut kondisi darurat atau kebutuhan setara darurat yang mengancam jiwa, belum adanya bahan halal dan suci, serta rekomendasi tenaga medis kompeten dan tepercaya. Assessing a medicine exception in necessity Treatment is clinically needed Check ingredients and suitable halal, pure alternatives A suitable alternative is available Use that alternative; reassess whether necessity still applies. No suitable alternative is available A qualified health professional assesses the need and recommends treatment. MUI Fatwa No. 30/2013 describes necessity or equivalent life-threatening need, no halal and pure alternative, and a recommendation from a competent, trusted medical professional. Al-Razi Al-Zahrawi Ibn al-Nafis Ibn al-Baytar Al-Kindi Nasir al-Din al-Tusi Al-Farabi Ibn Rushd (Averroes) Al-Jazari Al-Idrisi Bersuci dan kebersihan Wudhu Menjaga wudhu Mandi wajib Tayamum Shalat Shalat berjamaah Keringanan shalat Puasa Ramadan Zakat Haji dan umrah Pengurusan jenazah Purification and cleanliness Wudu Maintaining wudu Ghusl Tayammum Prayer Congregational prayer Prayer concessions Ramadan fasting Hajj and Umrah Funeral care . Purification of the Heart Learn to purify the heart, renew your intentions, and build good habits in daily life. These exercises are for reflection, not a measure of spiritual purity or a prescription of fixed practice counts. References are paraphrased. Fiqh of Worship A basic guide to purification, prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage, and everyday worship. Practical summaries follow the Shafi‘i school where specific details are discussed. The cited evidence gives general foundations, not every legal detail. Study special cases and differences among schools with a qualified teacher. Prophetic Biography Follow the Prophet’s ﷺ life from Makkah to the end of his life and reflect on its lessons in character. Events are arranged chronologically. Common Era dates are approximate, and some dates are disputed. Quranic and hadith references support the event or its lesson, not necessarily its exact date. Arabic Rhetoric (Balaghah) Study how expression fits meaning through grammar, morphology, ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘, with examples from the Qur’an. This introduction draws on general discussions of ma‘ani, bayan, and badi‘ and translations of Al-Balaghah al-Wadihah. Quranic rhetorical interpretation and its details should be taught and checked by a teacher; this summary does not replace a text or class. Islamic Marriage and Family Law A guide to engagement, marriage essentials, the mahr, spouses’ rights and duties, conflict resolution, and child custody. Based on summaries of Shafi‘i and majority-school family jurisprudence. Quranic and authentic hadith evidence is included as legal and ethical reference. Integrity and Anti-Corruption Islamic rulings on public trust, bribery, improper gifts, corruption, and protecting public wealth. Islam regards corruption as a grave sin that damages social justice. This material summarizes Quranic and authentic hadith evidence against unlawfully consuming public wealth. Islamic Transactions and Finance A guide to lawful earnings, riba, gharar, debts, Islamic business contracts, and contemporary services such as pay-later, online lending, and e-commerce. A foundational principle is that transactions are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material follows DSN-MUI guidance and contemporary Islamic commercial jurisprudence. Halal Food and Wholesome Living A guide to land and sea animals, Islamic slaughter, intoxicants and drugs, and critical points in processed foods. A foundational principle is that foods are permissible unless evidence establishes a prohibition. This material refers to LPPOM MUI halal standards and Shafi‘i jurisprudence. Islamic Medical Ethics and Contemporary Medicine Islamic guidance on seeking treatment, emergencies, blood and organ donation, euthanasia, IVF, and autopsies. An introduction based on MUI and International Islamic Fiqh Academy guidance and the objective of protecting life. Educational only: it is not a diagnosis or a substitute for advice from a doctor, pharmacist, or qualified scholar about an individual case. Comparative Religion: Tawhid and the Prophethood of Jesus A study of arguments for God’s oneness, the status of Jesus, Quranic and Biblical texts, the history of the Trinity, and prophecies of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Prepared from Quranic text, authentic hadith, Biblical quotations, and academic work in Christology. It aims to strengthen Islamic belief while supporting respectful, evidence-based interfaith dialogue. The Qur’an, Modern Science, and Natural Law Explore natural laws, relativity, Big Bang cosmology, the expanding universe, embryology, the water cycle, and ecological balance through Quranic signs. Draws on Quranic signs and established findings in physics, astronomy, and biology. It aims to encourage reflection on faith and creation. Islamic Creed and the Hereafter Study the pillars of faith, divine oneness and attributes, angels and the unseen, destiny, the Last Day, the grave, judgment, the bridge, Paradise, and Hell. Based on core Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama‘ah teachings and evidence from the Qur’an and authentic hadith. The aim is to strengthen faith and spiritual readiness for the Hereafter. Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence Learn the sources of Islamic law, why the four schools differ, and the five major legal maxims. Based on classical works such as Al-Waraqat by Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni and Shafi‘i legal maxims. The aim is to explain legal reasoning and encourage fairness toward legitimate scholarly disagreement. Hadith Studies and Authentication Understand hadith criticism, the structure of chains and texts, authentic and fabricated reports, and methods for checking narrations. Hadith terminology provides a rigorous method for evaluating historical reports and preserving the Prophetic message. The Golden Age of Islamic Civilization Explore global Muslim scholarship and civilization, from Baghdad’s House of Wisdom and al-Andalus to scholars who helped shape modern science. The centuries from the eighth to fourteenth CE show how Quranic learning and scientific and technological work flourished alongside one another. Islamic Parenting and Family Psychology Practical parenting guidance from the Qur’an and Sunnah: Luqman’s advice, child development, empathetic communication, digital safety, and family wellbeing. Children are a trust and are born upon a pure disposition. Islamic parenting nurtures them through loving example, prayer, and gentleness, not demands for obedience alone. Quranic Studies and Tafsir Methodology Study the compilation of the Qur’an, Makkan and Madinan passages, occasions of revelation, abrogation, and sound methods of interpretation. Quranic studies help readers understand revelation responsibly and guard against subjective readings or forcing a text into a context. Islamic Inheritance Law A guide to inheritance essentials, conditions and impediments, fixed-share heirs and residuaries, the 2:1 ratio, bequests, gifts, and dispute resolution. Inheritance law provides a framework for fair distribution of family wealth and helps prevent conflict. Digital Etiquette and Online Conduct Learn the manners of seeking knowledge online, responsible social media use, guarding speech, privacy, online backbiting, showing off, and digital copyright. In a fast-moving digital world, good manners and integrity distinguish mindful conduct from behavior driven by algorithms. Muslim Women: Exemplars and Fiqh Learn from the leadership, scholarship, and service of notable early Muslim women, alongside guidance on worship, menstruation, and women’s rights. Islam recognizes women’s independent property rights, access to knowledge, and meaningful contributions to society. Higher Objectives of Sharia and Governance Study the five higher objectives of Islamic law, the Constitution of Madinah, criminal law principles, consultation, and public leadership. Islamic law seeks genuine public benefit and aims to prevent oppression and harm for all people. End-Times Trials: The Dajjal and the Return of Jesus Study authentic reports about end-times trials, the Dajjal’s traits and deception, the Mahdi, the Dajjal’s defeat, and protections for believers. Studying end-times trials is not for panic or speculative predictions. It should strengthen tawhid, guard against confusion, and encourage good deeds. Stories of the Prophets and Messengers Follow the stories of the 25 prophets and messengers and the account of Khidr, exploring prophetic lineage, miracles, the five Messengers of steadfast resolve, and lessons in da‘wah. The prophetic stories are more than accounts of the past: they offer examples of character, steadfast faith, and the preservation of revelation. Islam in the Indonesian Archipelago, Walisongo, and Habaib Lineages Explore Islam’s peaceful spread through the spice routes and Samudera Pasai, Walisongo’s approach to local culture, Ba ‘Alawi lineage, maritime kingdoms, and pesantren traditions. Islam in the Nusantara spread through trade, diplomacy, good character, and culturally aware teaching. The Ten Companions Promised Paradise Learn from the character, sacrifice, and leadership of ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise by the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions were the finest generation of this community. Their integrity and sincerity offer guidance for preserving faith amid later trials. Islamic Environmental Ethics Care for the Earth as a trust: water conservation, animal welfare, tree planting, preventing environmental harm, and sustainable stewardship. Today’s ecological crisis is not only scientific and technological; it is also a moral and spiritual challenge. Islam makes care for creation part of faithful stewardship. Islamic Da‘wah and Interfaith Communication Study Quranic persuasive communication, audience awareness, respectful interfaith dialogue, and service through action. Da‘wah is not coercion or condemnation. It conveys truth with wisdom, sound reasoning, gentle character, and respectful argument. Angels, Jinn, and the Unseen Learn about angels, jinn, satanic deception, the intermediate realm, and authentic Islamic spiritual protection. This material supports sound belief and guards against shirk, superstition, fortune-telling, and occult claims through the Qur’an and Sunnah. Scholarly Disagreement and Religious Moderation Understand why legal schools differ, the etiquette of disagreement, wasatiyyah, and ways to preserve Muslim unity. This course encourages broad understanding and patience in subsidiary matters, while avoiding blind partisanship and reckless accusations of disbelief. kelahiran Sekitar 570 M • Kelahiran dan masa kecil Makkah Muhammad ﷺ lahir di Makkah dan tumbuh sebagai anak yatim. Beliau berasal dari Bani Hasyim, bagian dari Quraisy. Setelah kehilangan ibu, beliau diasuh kakeknya, lalu pamannya Abu Thalib. Tanggal kelahiran secara rinci diperselisihkan; Al-Qur’an mengingatkan pemeliharaan Allah terhadap beliau ketika yatim. Ibrah: berikan perhatian nyata kepada anak yatim dan keluarga yang membutuhkan. 93/6 khadijah Sebelum kenabian • Keluarga dan amanah Makkah Khadijah menjadi istri dan pendukung penting Rasulullah ﷺ. Kehidupan beliau memperlihatkan kepedulian kepada keluarga dan orang lemah. Saat wahyu pertama datang, Khadijah menenangkan beliau dengan mengingatkan akhlak baiknya. Ibrah: bangun kepercayaan melalui kejujuran dan dukungan kepada keluarga. wahyu Sekitar 610 M • Wahyu pertama Makkah Wahyu pertama turun melalui Jibril ketika beliau berada di Gua Hira. Awal Surah Al-Alaq berisi perintah membaca dengan nama Tuhan. Khadijah membawa beliau menemui Waraqah bin Naufal setelah pengalaman tersebut. Ibrah: jadikan belajar sebagai ibadah yang disertai kerendahan hati. dakwah Masa Makkah • Dakwah dan keteguhan Makkah Seruan tauhid menghadapi penolakan dan tekanan dari sebagian Quraisy. Rasulullah diperintahkan memperingatkan kerabat terdekat. Para sahabat mempertahankan iman di tengah ujian; sebagian mencari perlindungan di Habasyah. Ibrah: sampaikan kebenaran dengan sabar dan pertimbangkan keselamatan orang lain. 26/214 thaif Masa Makkah • Ujian di Thaif Makkah Penolakan yang berat tidak menghapus kasih sayang beliau. Dalam riwayat Aisyah, beliau menceritakan penolakan yang dialami dan kedatangan malaikat gunung. Beliau berharap keturunan mereka kelak menyembah Allah. Ibrah: tahan dorongan membalas dan buka peluang perubahan. isra Sebelum hijrah • Isra dan Mi’raj Makkah Isra adalah perjalanan malam dari Masjidil Haram ke Masjidil Aqsa. Peristiwa Isra disebut dalam awal Surah Al-Isra. Riwayat Mi’raj menjelaskan pensyariatan shalat lima waktu; tanggal peristiwanya diperselisihkan. Ibrah: rawat shalat sebagai bagian penting kehidupan seorang Muslim. 17/1 hijrah 622 M / 1 H • Hijrah ke Madinah Madinah Hijrah membuka babak pembentukan masyarakat Muslim di Madinah. Rasulullah berhijrah bersama Abu Bakar dengan persiapan dan pertolongan Allah. Persaudaraan Muhajirin dan Ansar menguatkan kehidupan masyarakat baru. Ibrah: gabungkan tawakal, perencanaan, dan dukungan kepada pendatang. 9/40 badar 2 H • Perang Badar Madinah Badar menjadi peristiwa penting pada awal masa Madinah. Al-Qur’an mengingatkan pertolongan Allah pada Badar saat kaum Muslim dalam keadaan lemah. Pelajari konteks sejarah konflik bersama adab dan tanggung jawab, bukan sebagai pembenaran kekerasan pribadi. Ibrah: tetap rendah hati ketika berhasil dan jangan melupakan pertolongan Allah. 3/123 uhud 3 H • Perang Uhud Madinah Uhud mengandung pelajaran tentang ketaatan, ujian, dan pemulihan. Al-Qur’an membahas perselisihan dan ketidaktaatan yang terjadi dalam peristiwa ini. Musibah menjadi kesempatan evaluasi bersama tanpa meninggalkan tanggung jawab. Ibrah: patuhi kesepakatan yang baik dan evaluasi kekeliruan secara jujur. 3/152 khandaq 5 H • Perang Khandaq / Ahzab Madinah Madinah menghadapi pengepungan pasukan sekutu. Kaum Muslim menghadapi ketakutan dan ujian berat. Surah Al-Ahzab mengingatkan pertolongan Allah dalam menghadapi pasukan sekutu. Ibrah: kuatkan kerja sama dan ketabahan ketika menghadapi krisis. 33/9 hudaibiyah 6 H • Perjanjian Hudaibiyah Madinah Kesepakatan damai membuka jalan bagi perkembangan dakwah. Rasulullah dan para sahabat berangkat dengan tujuan umrah, kemudian berunding dengan Quraisy. Kesediaan memenuhi perjanjian menunjukkan kesabaran dan pandangan jangka panjang. Ibrah: pertimbangkan manfaat jangka panjang dalam menyelesaikan perselisihan. fathu 8 H • Fathu Makkah Madinah Rasulullah kembali ke Makkah dalam peristiwa pembebasan kota. Berhala di sekitar Ka’bah disingkirkan dan tauhid ditegakkan. Kemenangan perlu disertai penghambaan kepada Allah, bukan kesombongan. Ibrah: gunakan kemampuan untuk memperbaiki keadaan dan menjaga kehormatan sesama. wada 10 H • Haji Wada Akhir hayat Rasulullah menunaikan haji dan menyampaikan pesan kepada umat. Beliau menegaskan kehormatan jiwa dan harta manusia. Manasik beliau menjadi rujukan pelaksanaan haji. Ibrah: jaga hak orang lain dalam ucapan, tindakan, dan urusan harta. wafat 11 H / 632 M • Wafat di Madinah Akhir hayat Rasulullah ﷺ wafat; para sahabat menghadapi kehilangan yang besar. Abu Bakar mengingatkan bahwa Allah tetap hidup dan tidak mati. Risalah dilanjutkan melalui pengamalan Al-Qur’an dan Sunnah serta penyampaian ilmu dengan amanah. Ibrah: pilih satu teladan akhlak Nabi untuk diterapkan secara konsisten.

title: Ilmu Tajwid & Makhraj Huruf
description: Kaidah bacaan Al-Qur’an dan latihan pengucapan huruf hijaiyah.
text: tajweed tajwid makharij Semua Nun Sukun & Tanwin Mim Sukun Mad Qalqalah & Ghunnah Tafkhim & Tarqiq Waqaf Izhar Halqi إظهار حلقي ء هـ ع ح غ خ Membaca nun sukun (نْ) atau tanwin dengan jelas tanpa dengung ketika bertemu salah satu dari 6 huruf halqi (tenggorokan). Ucapkan نْ / tanwin dengan jelas, tidak ditahan, langsung masuk ke huruf berikutnya tanpa ghunnah. 1 harakat (pendek, tanpa tahan) مِنْهَا min-hā نْ bertemu هـ → dibaca jelas عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ 'adzābun alīm tanwin bertemu ء → dibaca jelas غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ ghafūrun ḥalīm tanwin bertemu ح → dibaca jelas Menahan bacaan dengan dengung seperti ikhfa, atau memutus suara terlalu keras. Idgham Bighunnah إدغام بغنة ي ن م و Meleburkan nun sukun/tanwin ke huruf berikutnya disertai dengung (ghunnah). Hurufnya terkumpul dalam kata يَنْمُو. LeBURkan نْ ke huruf ي ن م و sambil dengungkan dari hidung sekitar 2 harakat. 2 harakat dengan ghunnah مَنْ يَقُولُ may yaqūl نْ + ي → melebur + dengung عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ 'adzābum muhīn tanwin + م → melebur + dengung مِنْ وَالٍ miw wāl نْ + و → melebur + dengung Tidak mendengung, atau mendengung terlalu panjang lebih dari 2 harakat. Idgham Bilaghunnah إدغام بلا غنة ل ر Meleburkan nun sukun/tanwin ke huruf ل atau ر TANPA dengung. Masukkan نْ sepenuhnya ke ل / ر, dibaca tegas tanpa suara hidung. 1 harakat, tanpa ghunnah مِنْ لَدُنْهُ mil ladunh نْ + ل → melebur tanpa dengung غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ ghafūrur raḥīm tanwin + ر → melebur tanpa dengung Ikut mendengung seperti bighunnah, atau tidak melebur sempurna. Iqlab إقلاب ب Mengubah bunyi nun sukun/tanwin menjadi mim (مْ) ketika bertemu huruf ب, disertai ghunnah. Ubah نْ menjadi bunyi مْ samar, bibir merapat ringan, dengungkan 2 harakat. Ditandai mim kecil (م) di mushaf. مِنْۢ بَعْدِ mim ba'd نْ + ب → berubah jadi مْ + dengung سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ samī'um baṣīr tanwin + ب → berubah jadi مْ Bibir merapat terlalu rapat hingga jadi mim murni, atau tidak mendengung. Ikhfa Haqiqi إخفاء حقيقي ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك Menyamarkan bunyi nun sukun/tanwin antara izhar dan idgham disertai ghunnah ketika bertemu 15 huruf sisanya. Siapkan lidah ke makhraj huruf berikutnya, samarkan نْ sambil dengungkan 2 harakat. Tebal/tipis mengikuti huruf setelahnya. مِنْ سُوءٍ ming sū' نْ + س → samar + dengung tipis عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ 'ang ṣalātihim نْ + ص → samar + dengung tebal كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ kirāmang kātibīn tanwin + ك → samar + dengung Dibaca jelas seperti izhar, atau melebur penuh seperti idgham. Ikhfa Syafawi إخفاء شفوي Menyamarkan mim sukun (مْ) ketika bertemu ب disertai ghunnah. Rapatkan bibir ringan tanpa menekan kuat, samarkan مْ sambil dengung 2 harakat. وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ wa hum bil-ākhirah مْ + ب → samar + dengung تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ tarmīhim biḥijārah Menekan bibir terlalu kuat hingga jadi mim murni, atau tidak dengung. Idgham Mimi / Mitslain إدغام متماثلين Meleburkan mim sukun ke mim berharakat berikutnya disertai ghunnah. Gabungkan dua م jadi satu tasydid, dengungkan 2 harakat. لَهُمْ مَا lahum mā مْ + م → melebur + dengung فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ fī qulūbihim maraḍ مْ + م → tasydid + dengung Tidak mendengung atau memutus antara dua mim. Izhar Syafawi إظهار شفوي selain م dan ب Membaca mim sukun dengan jelas ketika bertemu semua huruf selain م dan ب. Ucapkan مْ jelas tanpa dengung dan tanpa menahan. لَهُمْ فِيهَا lahum fīhā مْ + ف → jelas (hati-hati jangan samar) أَلَمْ تَرَ alam tara مْ + ت → jelas Menyamarkan مْ sebelum ف dan و hingga terdengar seperti ikhfa. Mad Thobi'i مد طبيعي ا Bacaan panjang dasar 2 harakat: fathah + alif, dhammah + wawu mati, kasrah + ya mati. Panjangkan 2 ketukan secara konsisten, tidak lebih. 2 harakat قَالَ qāla fathah + ا → 2 harakat يَقُولُ yaqūl dhammah + و → 2 harakat قِيلَ qīla kasrah + ي → 2 harakat Dipanjangkan lebih dari 2 harakat atau dibaca pendek 1 harakat. Mad Wajib Muttasil مد واجب متصل mad + hamzah 1 kata Mad thobi'i bertemu hamzah dalam SATU kata, wajib dipanjangkan. Panjangkan 4–5 harakat (pilih konsisten). 4–5 harakat السَّمَاءِ as-samā' ا + ء satu kata → 4-5 harakat سُوءَ sū' و + ء satu kata → 4-5 harakat Hanya dibaca 2 harakat seperti mad thobi'i biasa. Mad Jaiz Munfasil مد جائز منفصل mad + hamzah beda kata Mad thobi'i di akhir kata bertemu hamzah di awal kata berikutnya, boleh dibaca 2, 4, atau 5 harakat. Pilih 2 / 4 / 5 harakat dan konsisten dalam sekali bacaan. 2, 4, atau 5 harakat إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ innā a'ṭaināk ا akhir kata + ء awal kata لَا أَعْبُدُ lā a'bud boleh 2/4/5 harakat Tidak konsisten panjang-pendek dalam satu bacaan. Mad Lazim مد لازم mad + sukun asli Mad bertemu sukun asli (bukan karena waqaf). Wajib dibaca 6 harakat. Ada kilmi (kata) dan harfi (huruf pembuka surah). Panjangkan penuh 6 harakat, baik mutsaqqal (tasydid) maupun mukhaffaf. 6 harakat (wajib) الضَّالِّينَ aḍ-ḍāllīn kilmi mutsaqqal → 6 harakat آلْآنَ āl-ān kilmi mukhaffaf → 6 harakat الم alif lām mīm Dibaca kurang dari 6 harakat. Mad 'Arid Lissukun مد عارض للسكون mad + waqaf Mad thobi'i bertemu huruf yang disukunkan karena waqaf (berhenti). Boleh 2, 4, atau 6 harakat. Saat waqaf, pilih 2/4/6 harakat. Saat washal (lanjut) kembali 2 harakat. 2, 4, atau 6 harakat saat waqaf الْعَالَمِينَ al-'ālamīn waqaf di نْ → boleh 2/4/6 الرَّحِيمِ ar-raḥīm waqaf di مْ → boleh 2/4/6 Saat washal ikut dipanjangkan 6 harakat. Mad Lin مد لين وْ / يْ setelah fathah + waqaf Wawu/ya sukun didahului fathah lalu waqaf. Dibaca lembut, boleh 2/4/6 harakat. Lunakkan bacaan, jangan dipanjangkan kaku seperti mad thobi'i. قُرَيْشٍ quraisy يْ + waqaf → lembut الْخَوْفِ al-khauf وْ + waqaf → lembut Dibaca seperti mad thobi'i kaku atau terlalu pendek. Mad Iwad مد عوض tanwin fathah + waqaf Tanwin fathah (ً) yang diwaqafkan berubah menjadi mad 2 harakat, kecuali ta marbuthah (ة). Ganti tanwin fathah jadi fathah + alif 2 harakat. Ta marbuthah dibaca هْ mati. عَلِيمًا 'alīmā waqaf → alif 2 harakat رَحْمَةً raḥmah ta marbuthah → dibaca هْ, bukan iwad Tetap membaca tanwin (an) saat waqaf. Mad Shilah مد صلة هـ dhamir Ha dhamir (هُ / هِ) yang diapit huruf hidup: qashirah dibaca 2 harakat, thawilah (bertemu hamzah) 4-5 harakat. Panjangkan هُ jadi هُوْ dan هِ jadi هِيْ 2 harakat. Jika setelahnya hamzah → 4-5 harakat. 2 harakat (qashirah), 4-5 (thawilah) إِنَّهُ كَانَ innahū kān هُ diapit hidup → 2 harakat لَهُ أَجْرُهُ lahū ajruh thawilah → 4-5 harakat Tidak memanjangkan ha dhamir sama sekali. Qalqalah قلقلة Pantulan suara pada 5 huruf (ق ط ب ج د, singkatan قُطْبُ جَدٍّ) ketika sukun. Sughra: di tengah kata. Kubra: saat waqaf (lebih kuat). Pantulankan dengan jelas, jangan sampai terdengar seperti berharakat penuh. Kubra lebih memantul dari sughra. Pantulan seketika (tidak dihitung harakat) يَقْطَعُونَ yaqṭa'ūn قْ tengah → sughra الْفَلَقِ al-falaq waqaf di قْ → kubra مَسَدٍ masad waqaf di دْ → kubra Pantulan terlalu lemah (hilang) atau terlalu kuat hingga jadi harakat. Ghunnah غنة نْ / مْ bertasydid, idgham, iqlab, ikhfa Dengung dari hidung (khaishum) 2 harakat. Wajib pada nun/mim bertasydid (أَشَدّ), lalu idgham bighunnah, iqlab, ikhfa. Alirkan suara ke hidung 2 ketukan. Tingkatan terkuat: نّ dan مّ. إِنَّ inna نّ → ghunnah wajib terkuat ثُمَّ tsumma مّ → ghunnah wajib terkuat مِنْ بَعْدِ iqlab → ghunnah 2 harakat Dengung dari tenggorokan/mulut bukan hidung, atau durasi kurang dari 2 harakat. Tafkhim & Tarqiq (Ra & Lam Jalalah) تفخيم وترقيق ل (lafzhul jalalah) Ra dibaca tebal (tafkhim) saat fathah/dhammah, tipis (tarqiq) saat kasrah. Lam pada lafazh Allah tebal jika didahului fathah/dhammah, tipis jika kasrah. Mengikuti harakat huruf رَبِّ rabb رَ fathah → tebal رِجَالٌ rijāl رِ kasrah → tipis وَاللَّهُ wallāh lam jalalah setelah fathah → tebal بِاللَّهِ billāh lam jalalah setelah kasrah → tipis Ra selalu dibaca tebal, atau lam jalalah selalu tipis. Tanda Waqaf علامات الوقف م ۚ ۖ ۗ ۘ ∴ Rambu berhenti/menyambung: م (lazim/wajib berhenti), ۚ (jaiz/tsaw; berhenti lebih utama), ۖ (murakhkhash; lanjut lebih utama), ۗ (tidak boleh berhenti), ∴ (berhenti di salah satu titik). Ikuti tanda di mushaf agar makna tidak terputus. Waqaf qabih (buruk) bisa merusak makna. Berhenti dengan sukun + nafas … م … waqaf lazim wajib berhenti … ۚ … waqaf jaiz boleh berhenti/lanjut, berhenti lebih baik … ۗ … la waqfa jangan berhenti Berhenti sembarangan di tengah makna hingga mengubah arti ayat. Pangkal tenggorokan ء ه hamzah ha Hamzah dan ha keluar dari bagian tenggorokan paling dalam. أَ إِ أُ • هَ هِ هُ Hamzah terputus tegas; ha mengalir. Jangan menyamakan ه dengan ح.
